text: {"frames":["The cat on the windowsill sneezes three times, and the sails of the Tower mill begin to turn although not one flag on the dyke moves. Gareth the mapmaker stands below with ink on his thumb and a canal on his paper that nobody has ever seen. The miller's wife calls up that the mill only rests when its left gear, with fourteen oak cogs, and its right gear, with sixteen, are set in the right order. If the mill keeps turning, the water in the canal will climb over the cheese market by morning. Which sign must stand between the 14 on the left gear and the 16 on the right so that the mill can finally rest?","Marijke tips a jar of fog over the sleeping clog-maker's roof, and the fog climbs back up the stairs of the Tower like a cat that has changed its mind. On the left shelf stand fourteen jars of silver fog, and on the right stand sixteen jars of grey fog that smell of herring. The fog in the jars has begun to knock from the inside, and a small wooden ladle keeps stirring by itself. Marijke has to pour the right fog into the right canal before the ice on the canal starts to sing. Which sign must stand between the fourteen jars on the left and the sixteen jars on the right?","A creak of rope, then a soft bump, and every window of the crooked house with the hoist beam begins to glow yellow. Sieta the lock-keeper's girl stands in the square with a basket of waffles and watches the lamplight move from room to room, though the door is still bolted from the outside. The house has fourteen small windows on the canal side and sixteen on the market side, and each glows a little brighter than the last. The bolt will slide back only when the windows show the right amount to the stork on the roof. Which sign must stand between the 14 windows on the canal side and the 16 on the market side?","The bell of the drowned village rings at midnight, a time when no bell has rung for a hundred years, and Fenna's rope comes up wet to her elbows. Behind her on the dyke, a new shadow lifts off the wall and runs across the canal toward the Tower, long-legged and quick. Fenna has to ring the bell as many times as the shadow has steps, and the shadow has counted fourteen steps so far while the bell has rung sixteen. The shadow will rest on the Tower wall for good if the ringing does not match its steps. Which sign must stand between the 14 steps of the shadow and the 16 rings of the bell?","Joop the talking stork wants one thing more than anything in the world, and that is the map of the canal that nobody remembers. He has tricked the old lockmaster into lending it to him for a single night, and now he crouches on the Tower's top floor, tapping the paper with his beak. The map shows fourteen locks along the lost canal, but a second copy, folded in the drawer, shows sixteen. Joop must decide which copy to hand back before dawn, or the lockmaster will know he has cheated. Which sign must stand between the 14 locks on the first map and the 16 locks on the second?"]}
